Also known as: AUM
Definition: The total market value of the investments that an organisation manages for its clients.
The gain or loss on an investment or portfolio over a period, usually shown as a percentage of its starting value.
How much the value of an investment moves up and down over time.

Also known as: NII
Definition: The interest a bank earns on loans and investments minus the interest it pays on deposits and borrowing.

Also known as: NIM
Definition: The net interest income shown as a percentage of the bank's earning assets. It shows how profitable lending is.

Also known as: Lending Spread; Yield Spread
Definition: The difference between the average rate earned on loans and the average rate paid on deposits.

Also known as: Fee Income; Other Income; Fees and Commission Income
Definition: Income a bank earns from fees, commissions and trading rather than from interest.

Also known as: Efficiency Ratio; Cost-Income Ratio; CIR
Definition: The bank's running costs shown as a percentage of its income. A lower figure means the bank is more efficient.

Also known as: Bank ROA; Return on Average Assets; ROAA
Definition: The bank's profit shown as a percentage of its total assets.

Also known as: Bank ROE; Return on Average Equity; ROAE
Definition: The bank's profit shown as a percentage of shareholders' funds.

Also known as: Gross Loans; Total Loans; Loans and Advances
Definition: The total amount of loans a bank has lent out and not yet been repaid.

Also known as: Credit Growth; Loan Book Growth; Lending Growth
Definition: How much the loan book has grown compared with an earlier period.

Also known as: Deposits Growth; Deposit Base Growth
Definition: How much the money held in customer deposits has grown compared with an earlier period.

Also known as: Customer Deposits; Deposit Base; Deposits
Definition: The total money held by customers in accounts at the bank.

Also known as: LDR; Loans to Deposits
Definition: The loans a bank has made shown as a percentage of the deposits it holds. A very high figure may mean it relies on other funding.

Also known as: Current and Savings Account Ratio; Low Cost Deposit Ratio; CASA
Definition: The share of deposits held in current and savings accounts, which are cheaper for the bank than fixed deposits.

Also known as: NPL; NPA; Bad Loans; Non-Performing Assets
Definition: Loans where the borrower has stopped paying interest or repayments for a set time, usually 90 days.

Also known as: NPL Ratio; Gross NPA Ratio; Gross NPA
Definition: The non-performing loans shown as a percentage of total loans.

Also known as: Net Non-Performing Assets; Net NPL Ratio
Definition: The non-performing loans left after provisions have been set against them, shown as a percentage of net loans.

Also known as: PCR; Loan Loss Coverage; Coverage Ratio
Definition: The money set aside for bad loans shown as a percentage of the non-performing loans.

Also known as: Impairment Charge; Provisions for Bad Debts; Credit Loss Expense
Definition: The amount charged to profit in a period for loans that may not be repaid.

Also known as: Credit Cost; Cost of Risk; Credit Loss Ratio
Definition: The loan loss charge shown as a percentage of average loans.

Also known as: Loan Write-Offs; Charge-Off Rate; Net Charge-Offs
Definition: The share of loans that the bank has given up on and removed from its books.

Also known as: Past Due Rate; Arrears Rate; Overdue Loans
Definition: The share of loans where payments are late.

Also known as: DPD; Overdue Days; Arrears Days
Definition: The number of days a loan payment is late.

Also known as: Probability of Default; Default Ratio
Definition: The share of borrowers who fail to repay their loans as agreed.

Also known as: LGD; Loss Severity
Definition: The share of the loan amount that the lender expects to lose if the borrower fails to repay.

Also known as: EAD
Definition: The amount a lender expects to be owed at the time the borrower fails to repay.

Also known as: CRAR; Total Capital Ratio
Definition: The bank's capital shown as a percentage of its risk-weighted assets. Regulators set a minimum to make sure banks can absorb losses.

Also known as: CET1; CET1 Ratio; Tier 1 Ratio
Definition: The bank's highest-quality capital shown as a percentage of its risk-weighted assets.

Also known as: RWA; Risk Weighted Assets
Definition: The bank's assets adjusted for how risky each one is, used to work out how much capital the bank must hold.

Also known as: Bank Leverage Ratio
Definition: The bank's core capital shown as a percentage of its total exposure, without adjusting for risk.

Also known as: LCR
Definition: Whether the bank holds enough easy-to-sell assets to cover its cash needs for the next 30 days of stress.

Also known as: NSFR
Definition: Whether the bank's long-term funding is stable enough to support its long-term assets over a one-year period.

Also known as: New Accounts Opened; Account Openings; New Customers Banking
Definition: The number of new customer accounts opened in a period.

Also known as: Account Activity Rate
Definition: The number of accounts that have had activity, such as a transaction, within a set recent period.

Also known as: Products per Customer; Product Penetration; Cross Holding
Definition: The average number of products each customer holds with the bank.

Also known as: Mobile Banking Users; Digital Active Users; Online Banking Adoption
Definition: The share of customers who use online or mobile banking.

Also known as: Digital Transactions; Self-Service Transactions; Branch Transaction Share
Definition: The share of all transactions that are made through digital channels instead of branches or calls.

Also known as: Number of Transactions; Payment Volume; Transactions Processed
Definition: The number of transactions processed in a period.

Also known as: Payment Value; Total Transaction Value; Value of Payments
Definition: The total money value of the transactions processed in a period.

Also known as: Payment Success Rate; Transaction Failure Rate; Failed Transactions
Definition: The share of attempted transactions that went through successfully.

Also known as: Card Turnover; Card Spending; Card Transaction Value
Definition: The total amount customers spent using the bank's cards.

Also known as: Cards Activated; Card Usage Rate; Active Cards
Definition: The share of issued cards that customers have started to use.

Also known as: Interchange Fees; Card Fee Income; Merchant Fee Income
Definition: The fees the bank earns each time its cards are used to pay a merchant.

Also known as: Approval Rate; Acceptance Rate Loans; Applications Approved
Definition: The share of loan applications that the bank approved.

Also known as: Time to Decision; Loan Processing Time; Time to Disburse
Definition: The average time between a customer applying for a loan and getting a decision or the money.

Also known as: LTV Ratio; Loan-to-Value
Definition: The amount of a loan shown as a percentage of the value of the asset bought with it, such as a house.

Also known as: DSCR; Debt Coverage Ratio
Definition: The income available to pay debts divided by the amount of debt payments due. Above 1 means income covers the payments.

Also known as: Recovery Rate; Collections Rate; Loan Recovery Rate
Definition: The share of money due from borrowers that was actually collected.

Also known as: Bank NPS; Customer Recommend Score Bank
Definition: How likely customers are to recommend the bank to others.

Also known as: Business per Branch; Revenue per Branch; Branch Profitability
Definition: The business, such as deposits and loans, or the profit generated by each branch.

Also known as: Business per Employee; Profit per Employee Bank; Revenue per Employee Bank
Definition: The business or profit per bank employee.

Also known as: AML Alerts; Suspicious Transaction Alerts; AML Cases
Definition: The number of transactions flagged as possibly linked to money laundering and sent for review.

Also known as: SAR; STR; Suspicious Transaction Reports
Definition: The number of reports filed with the authorities about transactions that look suspicious.

Also known as: KYC Compliance; Know Your Customer Completion; KYC Refresh Rate
Definition: The share of customers whose identity checks are complete and up to date.

Also known as: Fraud Loss Rate; Fraud Rate Banking; Fraud Cases
Definition: The money lost to fraud in a period, often shown as a percentage of transaction value.

Also known as: NAV
Definition: The value of a fund's assets minus what it owes, usually shown per unit or share.

Also known as: NAV per Unit; NAV per Share; Unit Price
Definition: The net asset value of a fund divided by the number of units, which is the price at which units are bought and sold.

Also known as: AUA; Assets Under Custody; AUC
Definition: The value of the assets that a firm looks after for clients, without necessarily managing the investment decisions.

Also known as: Net Inflows; Net Sales Funds; Net New Money
Definition: The money invested in a fund or platform minus the money withdrawn in a period.

Also known as: Gross Sales Funds; Subscriptions; Total Inflows
Definition: The total money coming into a fund or platform before withdrawals are taken off.

Also known as: Outflows; Withdrawals; Fund Redemptions
Definition: The money withdrawn by investors from a fund in a period.

Also known as: Management Fee Income; Advisory Fee; Fee Revenue
Definition: The fee charged to investors for managing their money, usually a percentage of the assets managed.

Also known as: Fee Rate; Average Fee Rate; Revenue Yield
Definition: The fee income shown as a percentage of average assets under management.

Also known as: Total Expense Ratio; TER; Ongoing Charges Figure; OCF
Definition: The yearly cost of running a fund shown as a percentage of the fund's assets.

Also known as: Excess Return; Active Return; Outperformance
Definition: The return that an investment earned above its benchmark, after allowing for risk.

Also known as: Market Sensitivity; Market Beta
Definition: How much an investment moves when the market moves. A beta of 1 means it moves in line with the market.

Also known as: Sharpe; Risk-Adjusted Return
Definition: The return earned above a risk-free rate for each unit of risk taken, measured by volatility. A higher figure means a better return for the risk.

Also known as: Sortino; Downside Risk-Adjusted Return
Definition: Similar to the Sharpe ratio but it counts only downside swings as risk.

Also known as: Max Drawdown; Peak to Trough; Drawdown
Definition: The biggest fall in value from a peak to the lowest point before a new peak was reached.

Also known as: Active Risk; Tracking Difference
Definition: How much a portfolio's returns differ from those of its benchmark.

Also known as: Return Volatility; Std Dev
Definition: A measure of how much returns vary around their average. A higher figure means a bumpier ride.

Also known as: VaR
Definition: The largest loss that a portfolio is expected to suffer over a set period at a set level of confidence, such as 95%.

Also known as: Index Return; Benchmark Performance; Market Return
Definition: The return of the market index or reference portfolio used to judge how an investment performed.

Also known as: TWR; Time Weighted Rate of Return
Definition: A return measure that removes the effect of money being added or withdrawn, so it shows how the investments performed.

Also known as: MWR; Internal Rate of Return Portfolio; Dollar-Weighted Return
Definition: A return measure that takes into account the timing and size of money added or withdrawn.

Also known as: Annualized Return; CAGR; Compound Annual Growth Rate
Definition: The yearly rate of return that would give the same overall result as the actual returns over the period.

Also known as: Income Yield; Distribution Yield
Definition: The yearly dividends paid per share shown as a percentage of the share price.

Also known as: PE Ratio; P/E; Earnings Multiple
Definition: The share price divided by the earnings per share. It shows how much investors pay for each unit of profit.

Also known as: EPS; Basic EPS; Diluted EPS
Definition: The company's profit divided by the number of shares, showing the profit that belongs to each share.

Also known as: Portfolio Mix; Allocation; Asset Mix
Definition: The way a portfolio is split between asset types such as shares, bonds and cash.

Also known as: Top Holdings Share; Concentration Risk; Top 10 Holdings
Definition: How much of a portfolio is held in its largest few investments.

Also known as: Turnover Ratio; Fund Turnover; Trading Turnover
Definition: How much of a portfolio is bought and sold in a year, which affects trading costs.

Also known as: Modified Duration; Interest Rate Sensitivity; Bond Duration
Definition: How sensitive the price of a bond or bond portfolio is to a change in interest rates, shown in years.

Also known as: Bond Rating
Definition: A grade given by a rating agency showing how likely a borrower is to repay, which helps judge the risk of a bond.

Also known as: YTM; Bond Yield; Redemption Yield
Definition: The total return expected on a bond if it is held until it matures and all payments are made as promised.
